newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes hold steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges softer, cargoes hold steady.

text.p: Fuel oil barges were a touch weaker on Wednesday as thin demand pressured prices lower.
High sulphur barges traded at $95 and $96 fob ARA and low sulphur barges were talked at $103-106 fob ARA.

The high sulphur cracked cargo market continued to suffer from tight supplies and support was seen from the Portuguese tender, but prices were hovering around $100 fob NWE and not moving up to the $104.50 fob paid last week.
A small 10-15,000 tonne cargo of high density high sulphur cracked material was attracting at least five interest buyers although prices were not discussed.
Some dealers thought high sulphur may come under pressure in the first week of September as traders try to buy up product to sell into Portugal.
Low sulphur cracked was more active than high sulphur with a short into a U.K utility understood to have been covered. A small private deal was also concluded.

Product into Italy were assessed around $111-113 cif Italy with the Caribbean a good source for material. A northern cargo was understood to be offered around $105 fob. A Portuguese requirement for up to 80,000 tonnes has still not been met.
